description: SPECIAL NOTICE: VENDORS MUST REFERENCE THE NOTICE ID WHEN SUBMITTING A CAPABILITY STATEMENT. NASA/NSSC intends to issue a sole source contract to BARKLEY CONSULTING GROUP LLC 34 Spencer LN Stony Brook, New York 11790-3139 United States under the authority of FAR 12.102(a). It has been determined that BARKLEY CONSULTING GROUP LLC is the sole provider of virtual instructor-led delivery of one (1) course delivered as a dedicated cohort session for up to twenty-seven (27) Government participants. Delivery will be conducted live via Zoom (or Zoom for Government when required) and will include digital course materials, instructor-led facilitation, and Barkley Consulting Group logistics/program support. NASA/NSSC will be the procuring center for this effort. Performance will be located at NASA/ Headquarters (HQ). The Government intends to acquire Commercial items or services using the provisions, clauses and procedures prescribed in FAR Part 12 for Commercial The NAICS Code for this procurement is 611430. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort in writing to the identified point of contact not later than 12:00 p.m. Central Standard Time on 10/26/2026. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed effort on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. NOTE: Quotes received in response to this notice will NOT be considered and will not be evaluated by NASA�s Technical End User Team. title: Request for Information Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense Avenger Weapon System Support
description: Request for Information Project Manager, Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense Avenger Weapon System Support Synopsis: The Short and Intermediate Effectors for Layered Defense (SHIELD) Project Office is conducting market research to determine if there are potential sources with the capability to provide engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201 (e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. The Government Point of Contact will be Ms. Lillian Irby, U.S. Army Contracting Command-Redstone, and can be contacted via email: lillian.m.irby.civ@army.mil. EMAIL ONLY, NO PHONE CALLS. Administrative: In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not an offer and cannot be accepted by the U.S. Government to form a binding contract. No contract award is intended as a result of this request. The U.S. Government will not pay for information received. Per FAR 52.215-3, Request for Information (RFI) or Solicitation for Planning Purposes: a. The U.S. Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this RFI or to otherwise pay for the information solicited, except as an allowable cost under other contracts as provided in subsection 31.205-18, bid and proposal costs, of the FAR. b. Although the term �proposal� may be used in this RFI, your response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. c. This RFI is for planning and market research purposes only and should not be considered as a request for proposals or as a solicitation to do business with the U.S. Government. Avenger System Overview: The Avenger mission is to provide a lightweight, highly mobile, shoot-on-the-move, day/night, short-range surface-to-air missile and gun weapon system. Mounted on an M1097A2 High Mobility Multi-Purpose Wheeled Vehicle (HMMWV), it engages Fixed Wing, Rotary Wing, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle, and Cruise Missile threats. The Avenger M47A2 derivative system, termed Slew-to-Cue, receives cues to a track from an outside source and automatically slews to and follows the target beyond the line of sight. Avenger System Description: The Avenger Weapon System is a critical component of the Army�s Short Range Air Defense System (SHORADS). The system consists of: Two Standard Vehicle Mounted Launchers mounted on a turret A .50 caliber machinegun Forward Looking Infrared Laser Range Finder Environmental Control Unit/Prime Power Unit Auto-track systems and Identification Friend or Foe system Two 12V, 100 AMP lead-acid batteries connected in series (24V system power) 360 degrees continuously rotating, gyro-stabilized turret mounted on the HMMWV The fire unit can engage targets with missiles or the machinegun while on-the-move or stationery. The gunner can operate the system in-turret or from a remote location using the Remote-Control Unit. Scope of Work and Contractor Requirements: The SHIELD Project Office is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive engineering and technical services in support of the Avenger Weapon System and all derivative systems. Note: Proposers must have the required capability at the start of the performance period and must be able to perform all required tasks. Partial solution proposals will not be considered. Core Support Areas: The contractor will be responsible for complex system engineering, manufacturing, test equipment, logistics, and sustainment support. Support includes, but is not limited to: Engineering and Integration: Providing detailed technical expertise for Avenger Weapon Systems, Line Replaceable Units (LRU) (all variants), support equipment, and system interfaces. Designing and fabricating new solutions based on the current Avenger design to meet U.S. Government requirements. Performing complex system integration tasks. Providing software engineering and development for current and future software requirements. Providing in-depth system engineering analysis to support performance improvement, failure analysis, and other engineering activities. Testing & Analysis: Supporting test activities, including the assessment of test results. Providing design and technical support for existing and future contractor- and U.S. Government-owned test equipment. Performing reliability assessments and failure analysis with corrective action identification at the system and LRU level. Quickly and effectively analyzing and resolving hardware/software failures to restore operational capability. Logistics: Performing logistics functions, including technical manual generation/modification, maintenance support, system repairs and Field Service Representative support. Training and Fielding: Redesigning, replacing, installing, and training on all LRUs. Conducting training and system deployment, including New Equipment Training. Supporting sustainment training for deployed systems. Quality Assurance and Security: Complying with all Quality Assurance requirements (configuration management). Maintaining a facility compliant with all federal, state, and local requirements. Ensuring compliance with current DoW Information Assurance and Cybersecurity requirements. Meeting all contractor security, Communications Security, Federal, and DoW requirements, including Defense Security Service accreditation for both unclassified and classified information. Personnel Requirements: The U.S. Government requires a team of Field Service Representatives with expertise in Weapon Systems operation, sustainment, mechanical/electrical maintenance, physical security, and site maintenance. Security Clearance: Contractor employees will be required to hold and maintain a Secret security clearance. Operations: The contractor is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation and maintenance of Avenger Weapon Systems and sites. Provide a statement describing your company as domestically or foreign owned (if foreign owned, please indicate country of ownership). Part B. Capability Questionnaire: Capabilities Overview: Briefly describe your company�s capabilities, the nature of your goods/services, staff composition, and management structure. Past Experience: Describe up to five previous projects similar in complexity to this requirement. Include contract numbers, a brief description of work, period of performance, supported agency/organization, and individual points of contact (Contracting Officer or Program Manager). Defense Systems and Avenger Experience: What experience do you have planning and executing the deployment and sustainment of weapons/defense systems? title: Sources Sought: IEE Capability for FFP Non-Personal Healthcare Services � Up to Two (2) OB/GYN Physician Full-Time Equivalent Positions, Pine Ridge Service Unit, Pine Ridge IHS Hospital, Pine Ridge, SD
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE (MARKET RESEARCH ONLY) Notice Number: IHS1528550 Title: Sources Sought: IEE Capability for FFP Commercial Non-Personal Healthcare Services � Up to Two (2) OB/GYN Physician Full-Time Equivalent Positions, Pine Ridge Service Unit, Pine Ridge IHS Hospital, Pine Ridge, SD. 1.0 NOTICE TYPE This Sources Sought Notice is issued for informational and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation, request for quotation (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), obligation, or commitment by the Indian Health Service (IHS), U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The purpose of this notice is strictly to conduct market research to determine the availability and capability of Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs), and other responsible sources capable of performing the requirement described herein. Responses will be used to assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including the applicability of the Buy Indian Act (25 U.S.C. 47) and HHSAR Subpart 326.6, Acquisitions Under the Buy Indian Act. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561320 - Temporary Help Services). Respondents are specifically invited to recommend an alternative NAICS code if they believe another code more accurately reflects the principal purpose of this requirement. The anticipated Product Service Code (PSC) is Q507 - Medical - Obstetrics and Gynecology. 2.0 BACKGROUND This requirement is for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal healthcare services contract to provide qualified OB/GYN physicians for the Pine Ridge Service Unit (PRSU), Pine Ridge IHS Hospital, Pine Ridge, South Dakota. 3.0 OBJECTIVE The objective of this requirement is to obtain up to two (2) qualified OB/GYN physician Full-Time Equivalent (FTE) positions to support clinical operations at Pine Ridge IHS Hospital and associated PRSU facilities and to ensure the continuous delivery of medical services to the patient population served by the Pine Ridge Service Unit. 4.0 SCOPE The Contractor shall provide qualified OB/GYN physician services in accordance with the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS). All services shall be performed in compliance with applicable federal, state, tribal, and local laws and regulations, as well as applicable professional licensing, credentialing, privileging, accreditation, and facility requirements. 5.0 ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal healthcare services contract or order. The final contract type, pricing structure, and acquisition approach will be determined after completion of market research and development of the solicitation. 6.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE Base Period: Ten (10) weeks. Option Periods: Twenty-five (25) 10-week option periods, if exercised by the Government. Respondents are requested to comment on the commercial practicality of this period-of-performance structure in Section 9.0 below. 7.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Pine Ridge Service Unit / Pine Ridge Hospital PHS Indian Health Service P.O. Box 1201 East Highway 18 Pine Ridge, South Dakota 57770 Kyle Health Center P.O. Box 540 Kyle, South Dakota 57752 Wanblee Health Center P.O. Box 290 100 Clinic Drive Wanblee, South Dakota 57577 LaCreek Clinic Outlying Clinic Location Martin, South Dakota Mobile Medical Unit Typically parked at Pine Ridge Hospital and deployed throughout the Pine Ridge Reservation as needed. 8.0 PAYMENT / INVOICE SUBMISSION Any resulting award will require electronic submission of payment requests through the Department of the Treasury Invoice Processing Platform (IPP), or successor system, in accordance with HHSAR 352.232-71, Electronic Submission of Payment Requests. Additional invoicing instructions will be provided in any resulting solicitation and award. 9.0 CAPABILITY STATEMENT SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested parties are requested to submit capability statements demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement. Responses should be sufficiently detailed to support meaningful market research and should address the following, as applicable: 1. General Capability Assessment Provide a brief description of the respondent's understanding of the requirement, including perceived challenges, feasibility, and any innovative approaches or recommendations. 2. Relevant Experience and Performance History Current capability and capacity to perform similar work. Prior experience performing comparable healthcare staffing or physician services of similar scope and size. Organizational experience and management approach. Examples of relevant federal, state, tribal, or commercial contracts. 3. Technical Capability Provide evidence demonstrating the ability to furnish and sustain up to two (2) OB/GYN physician FTE positions and to meet the requirements described in the draft PWS, including recruitment, credentialing, privileging, scheduling, Regular Hours coverage, On-Call coverage, and continuity of care requirements. 4. Business Information Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). Organization name and address. Point of contact (name, phone, and email). Business size and socioeconomic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, etc.). Applicable NAICS code(s), including whether NAICS 561320 is appropriate for the principal purpose of this requirement. If another NAICS code is recommended, identify the code and provide a brief rationale. Indian Small Business Economic Enterprise (ISBEE) and/or Indian Economic Enterprise (IEE) status, if applicable, including whether the respondent is eligible to represent itself as an ISBEE and/or IEE for this acquisition. 5. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 339999 - All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing and PSC 7690 - Miscellaneous Printed Matter Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) USPTO is seeking a contractor who can fulfill the agency�s requirements for the following awards, certificates, medallions, as well as appropriate packaging and direct shipping for each. This requirement includes manufacturing, assembly and preparing the awards for delivery and shipping directly to the recipient or to an agency office as required. The Office of Human Resource (OHR) supports a variety of non-monetary awards to recognize and reward employee excellence. Superior performance is generally considered as the type of employee performance that contributes, directly or indirectly, to the mission of the USPTO. These non-monetary awards include Bronze Medal Awards, Career Achievement Awards which includes Distinguished Career Awards and Exceptional Career Awards, Retirement Certificates, Directors Award, Length of Service Award and Leadership in Action Award. These awards range in style and type to include framed certificates, medals encased in leucite and presented with a certificate and display box and laser etched clear crystal desktop awards. Note: Sample photos of the awards are attached in a pdf to this RFI 1) Bronze Medal Awards- This award is used to recognize an organization, group or individual employees who have made a major impact on the effectiveness of the USPTO. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity per year is up to 450. 2) Distinguished Career Awards: This award marks at least 20 years of superior performance as an employee of the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 150. 3) Exceptional Career Awards: This award marks at least ten (10) years of superior performance with the USPTO, with the last five (5) consecutive years demonstrating exceptional performance. The awards ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in June/July. The estimated quantity per year is up to 275. 4) Retirement Certificates: The purpose of this certificate is to recognize USPTO employees upon the occasion of their retirement. These are ordered/requested upon notification of an employee retiring. Framed certificates are created throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 120. 5) Directors Award: The purpose of this award is to recognize individuals and/or group recognition for contributions to the Agency, Managers, supervisors or other employees may nominate those whose contributions have far exceeded expectations or reflect positively on the USPTO. These awards are sporadic throughout the year. The estimated quantity per year is up to 100. 6) Leadership in Action Award. The recipients are recognized during the USPTO Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony. The Bronze Medal Awards Ceremony takes place annually and typically occurs in October. The estimated quantity of Leadership in Action awards is up to 400 per year. The three (3) award tiers are Supervisor of the Year (SOTY), Supervisor of the Year (SOTY) Finalist, Approved Nominated Supervisors. Each award tier has a different associated cost and quantity. 7) Length of Service Award: The purpose of this award is to recognized USPTO employee�s length of Federal service. This award is issued monthly. The estimated quantity per year is approximately 2,600. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of awards and services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. title: Palm Beach Harbor, South Jetty Rehabilitation 2026, Palm Beach County, Florida
description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking within the tolerances provided. Mobilization of equipment and the construction necessary to repair the jetty must be water-based and require the use of marine construction methods and equipment. Work on top of the jetty will be permitted. Land-based access to the project site will not be permitted. Rehabilitation also consists of concrete repairs to the South Jetty at Palm Beach Harbor as indicated on the drawings. Prior to work on the jetty, conduct a pre-construction benthic community survey on the jetty structure and any adjacent submerged areas that may be impacted by the Contractors operations. Complete any coral relocations required as a result of the benthic survey prior to jetty work. Field personnel conducting coral survey and transplantation activities must either be qualified relocation contractors by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission or must provide documentation of having successfully conducted relocation of corals in Florida. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 330 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). title: Sources Sought / Request for Information � BENEFEDS Federal Benefits Enrollment and Premium Administration Services (Follow-On)
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. It is not a solicitation, does not constitute a commitment by the Government, and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Responses will not be reimbursed. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is conducting market research for the follow-on acquisition of BENEFEDS, the Government-sponsored enrollment, premium and allotment administration, and customer service platform supporting the Federal Employees Dental and Vision Insurance Program (FEDVIP), the Federal Flexible Spending Account Program (FSAFEDS), and the Federal Long Term Care Insurance Program (FLTCIP). The anticipated requirement includes FEDVIP enrollment and eligibility services; premium and payroll-allotment administration across more than fifty payroll and annuity providers; a bilingual multi-channel contact center; education, communications, and Open Season support; the information systems, security authorization, privacy, accessibility, and continuity functions that underpin the services; reporting; fraud, waste, and abuse prevention; and transition-in and transition-out. The current contract, IDIQ 24322622D0006, was competitively awarded June 28, 2022; services for calendar year 2027 are being provided under a task order on that contract. OPM anticipates award of the follow-on in spring 2027 with full services beginning on or about December 31, 2027. OPM seeks (1) capability and business-size information from firms of all sizes, including small businesses in every socioeconomic category, to support its small business determination, and (2) industry comments on the anticipated requirement, the draft performance standards, the transition approach, and the contract structure � including anything OPM has not listed that a capable benefits administrator would expect to see specified. The attached notice describes the requirement and the information requested; Attachment 1 is the required response format. Questions about this notice are due by 3:00 p.m. ET, Wednesday, October 14, 2026, by email to James.Faulkner@opm.gov and Dennis.Hodges@opm.gov. Responses are due by 3:00 p.m. ET, Monday, October 26, 2026, by email to both addresses with the subject line "BENEFEDS SSN/RFI Response � [Company Name]". OPM may invite selected respondents to 30-minute virtual sessions during the week of November 2, 2026. title: Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic
description: N0016426SNBXX REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT Calibration services for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE) PSC J052, J066, H266, H366 NAICS 541380, 811219 1.0 Objective & Background This Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought (SS) notice is issued by the Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division Contracting Department, Crane, IN. The NSWC Crane Contracting Department is conducting market research to identify potential industry partners capable of providing comprehensive calibration services in accordance with OPNAV 3960.16 for a diverse inventory of Test, Measurement, and Diagnostic Equipment (TMDE). Currently, NSWC Crane utilizes organic support in combination with a SeaPort Task Order and a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for calibration of TMDE for navy programs at NSWC Crane. The Government is exploring the feasibility of consolidating these requirements into a single, multi-year contract (e.g., Base Year plus Option Years). The primary objective of this market research is to determine if industry is interested in running the calibration program in accordance with the OPNAV 3960.16 at the contractor's own facility or government owned contractor ran facility. The Government is seeking capability statements regarding the calibration of approximately 2,700 unique TMDE types and ~7,000 total TMDE assets annually to ensure operational readiness and strict compliance with technical standards. 2.0 Acquisition Strategy & Disclaimer THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Navy has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Information gathered from this market research will directly inform the Government's future acquisition strategy, including the determination of contract type, the feasibility of consolidating these calibration services, and the viability of shifting the primary place of performance to contractor-owned facilities. 3.0 Incumbent Contract Information The current workload is distributed across the following contract vehicles: Supported Equipment N0017819D8285/N0016423F3007 Goldbelt ILS 5/1/2023-4/30/2028 Unsupported Equipment N0016426A0026 Cross technologies 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0025 ENI 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0024 Transcat 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0023 Micro precision 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 N0016426A0022 Tektronix 4/1/2026-3/31/2031 4.0 Summary of Requirements The required calibration services span multiple asset categories. All calibration services must be performed in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025, navy approved and/or specialized approved procedures. Technical Standard & Location Requirements: The Government intends for the bulk of calibration services to be performed by the contractor at the contractor's facility. All calibrations must conform strictly to the ISO/IEC 17025 standard. While most calibration efforts will be conducted at contractor facilities and on station at NSWC Crane, there will be a significant amount of calibration workload that will be conducted at various industry locations supporting NSWC Crane workload. Locations vary across Indiana and adjoining states and are subject to change through the life of the contract. Logistics requirements: Personnel physically inspect the shipping container and the TMDE itself for transit damage. Onsite Pick up/delivery of assets 2-5 times per week Reference MIL-STD-2073-1 for assets over $10,000 Verifies that all components listed on the shipper's DD Form 1149 or stowage list are present. Engineering services: The Contractor shall provide high level support in Metrology and Calibration Laboratory for various project and programs at NSWC CRANE. Various Administration support: Contractors must maintain rigorous, auditable stewardship of all GFP throughout its lifecycle using the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) GFP Module. Workload Distribution The historical and projected annual workload includes, but is not limited to, the following functional shop code categories: Shop Code Category Estimated Annual Calibration Volume TORQUE - 1,219 METERS/D&A - 1,070 POWER SUPPLIES - 571 FIELD CAL (Onsite) - 341 HANDTOOLS - 275 PRESSURE/VACUUM - 175 MICROWAVE ACTIVE - 394 SIG GEN - 276 TEMP/HUMIDITY - 454 Other Specialized Equipment - ~2,000+ (Combined) 5.0 Submission Instructions Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a comprehensive capability statement addressing their ability to meet the workload requirements outlined in Section 4.0. Responses are due no later than 1400 EST on 26 October 2026 Submission Format Requirements Page Limit Responses shall be limited to 5 pages. Delivery Method Submissions must be sent via e-mail only to the designated Point of Contact. Proprietary Info Must be minimized and clearly marked. Please segregate proprietary information to aid the Government's review. Required Information to Include Interested parties are requested to submit a Capability Statement addressing the following key areas: Corporate Overview Company name, CAGE code, UEI, socio-economic status (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), SDVOSB), and current CMMC Certification Level. Contractor Facility Capacity Explicit confirmation of the vendor's ability to host and process this volume of equipment at their own facility, rather than relying on Government space. The contractor should be within distance capable of being here 2-5 a week. Technical Capability Overview of laboratory capabilities for the listed categories, current accreditations (e.g., ISO/IEC 17025, ANSI/NCSL Z540.1, ANSI/NCSL Z540.3), and capacity to maintain industry standard turnaround times (TAT) for high-volume throughput. Logistics and Handling Specific processes for managing the logistics pipeline: secure transportation, shipping/receiving of government assets, and the methodology for dispatching technicians for the ~340 required onsite (field) calibrations. Government Points of Contact Direct all questions regarding this RFI and submit all capability statements to the following designated point of contact: Primary POC: Andrew Figg andrew.n.figg.civ@us.navy.mil Secondary POC Anthony Morin anthony.m.morin5.civ@us.navy.mil 6.0 Attachments OPNAVINST 3960.16C List of Unique TMDE (Excel File)

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) BUILDING 215 ADVANCED MEASUREMENT LABORATORY (AML) CLEANROOM REPAIR AND HEPA FILTER REPLACEMENT Solicitation/Reference No.: 1333ND26RNB190014 1. PURPOSE OF THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is conducting market research pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and FAR 15.201 to obtain industry feedback concerning the scope, schedule, phasing, cleanroom outage requirements, technical and performance risks, and estimated construction cost associated with the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory (AML) Cleanroom Repair and HEPA Filter Replacement project. NIST previously solicited this requirement under Solicitation No. 1333ND26RNB190014. NIST did not receive an acceptable offer under that solicitation. NIST is therefore reassessing the requirement and acquisition approach before determining whether and how to resolicit the project. NIST is particularly interested in identifying aspects of the requirement that may materially affect industry participation, constructability, schedule feasibility, pricing, risk, or the ability of contractors to submit competitive proposals. Industry is encouraged to provide candid feedback and to identify recommended changes that could improve constructability, competition, schedule feasibility, cost certainty, and overall project execution while continuing to meet NIST�s mission and cleanroom operational requirements. 2. RFI / MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE THIS RFI IS ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND ACQUISITION PLANNING PURPOSES. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), INVITATION FOR BID (IFB), REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ), OR OTHER SOLICITATION. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses to this RFI. Responses will be treated as information only and shall not be construed as offers or proposals that can be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs incurred in preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI or for participating in any follow-up discussions. This RFI does not obligate the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government�s ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be used by NIST in developing or revising the acquisition strategy, statement of work, specifications, schedule, phasing requirements, outage requirements, Government cost estimate, and future solicitation. Respondents should clearly identify and mark any proprietary, confidential, or commercially sensitive information contained in their responses. Respondents should avoid including proprietary information unless necessary to provide a meaningful response. 3. PROJECT BACKGROUND The project involves repair and modernization work within the Building 215 Advanced Measurement Laboratory cleanroom located at the NIST Gaithersburg Campus. The AML cleanroom encompasses approximately 1,800 square meters and includes approximately 750 square meters of Class 100 cleanroom space. The facility supports sensitive NIST research activities and contains specialized and, in some instances, irreplaceable scientific equipment. The project generally includes, but is not limited to: Replacement of approximately 1,200 terminal supply HEPA filters; Repair and/or modification of HEPA filter connections; Testing, balancing, certification, and recertification of affected HEPA filters and cleanroom spaces; Replacement of approximately 70 variable air volume (VAV) terminal units; Replacement of approximately 54 airflow monitoring devices; Installation of approximately 32 exhaust air control valves; Modification and repair of associated ductwork; Rebalancing of associated air-handling and exhaust systems; Verification and repair, as required, of existing capped ductwork; Controls-related work; Cleaning, testing, balancing, commissioning, and cleanroom certification associated with each affected area; and Protection of existing cleanroom spaces, research operations, and sensitive scientific equipment throughout construction. Detailed project drawings, specifications, and/or relevant portions of the previously issued solicitation may be attached to this RFI or otherwise made available through SAM.gov for purposes of industry review. 4. CURRENT PHASING AND OUTAGE CONCEPT NIST�s previous acquisition strategy was developed to minimize disruption to ongoing research operations by performing the work through phased cleanroom outages rather than shutting down the entire cleanroom for the duration of construction. The previous requirement contemplated 19 construction phases consisting of 18 Critical Cleanroom Outage Phases and one Non-Critical Phase. For each Critical Cleanroom Outage Phase, the contemplated outage period was approximately nine calendar days, generally structured as follows: Outage/construction activities begin at approximately 7:00 p.m. on Friday; Work proceeds continuously, including 24-hour-per-day/seven-day-per-week operations, as necessary; Construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification are completed during the outage period; and The affected cleanroom area is required to achieve Ready for Re-Occupancy by approximately 7:00 a.m. on the second following Monday. Ready for Re-Occupancy generally means that required construction, startup, testing, balancing, cleaning, commissioning, and applicable cleanroom certification have been completed; the affected area is operationally capable of supporting its intended use without material restriction; and no deficiencies remain that materially impair safe occupancy or cleanroom operations. The previous requirement also contemplated maintaining unaffected cleanroom bays

title: CAAA Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) BOA
description: SECTION A � SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure the Rapid Acquisition Sustainment Program (RASP) supply requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 332710 (Machine Shops; Size Standard: 500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 0001 - RASP BOA Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 5340 (Hardware, Commercial). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a RASP BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future RASP orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) operations across the categories defined in Section B. Items ordered may include detailed specifications from controlled technical data packages referencing military specifications (MIL-SPEC) or restricted technical drawings. 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussions. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) The following unfunded CLINs are established at the master agreement level for administrative categorization only: CLIN 0001: Machined and Fabricated Metal Parts (NAICS 332710 / 332999) CLIN 0002: Plastics and Injection Molded Components (NAICS 326199) CLIN 0003: Wooden Containers, Boxes, and Pallets (NAICS 321920) CLIN 0004: Chemicals, Organic and Inorganic (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0005: Paints, Coatings, and Adhesives (NAICS 325510) CLIN 0006: Miscellaneous Hardware, Tools, and Gaskets (NAICS 332510) CLIN 0007: Other Class IX Sustainment Products SECTION C � CAAA RASP EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES A BOA is not a contract (FAR 16.703(a)). An order becomes a binding contract upon Government acceptance and award. The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability in at least one (1) supply category listed in Attachment 0001- RASP BOA Purchase Description by completing Attachment 0004 � Combined Technical and Past Performance Questionnaire. No site visits are required at this stage. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order RFQ. Detail PDs, TDPs, and QA requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. ALIGNMENT All supplies delivered under individual orders must support manufacturing and readiness at CAAA. Processes, tolerances, and quality controls must align with technical data packages (TDPs) provided at the order level. 2. JOINT CERTIFICAITON PROGRAM (JCP) Master BOA Level: To be eligible for a master BOA, and to maintain eligibility, the contractor must possess and maintain active JCP registration to access export-controlled TDPs and drawings. Verification: The Government will independently verify JCP status prior to execution. Failure to maintain active certification results in immediate termination of the BOA. Subcontractors: Prime contractors must ensure subcontractors are registered in the JCP if they require access to restricted drawings. Information Link: Procedures are available at the DLA Joint Certification Program (JCP) Website. 3. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the RASP BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 52.219-33): Non-manufacturers must supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer, unless an SBA class or individual waiver applies. The KO will monitor compliance at the order level. 5. LOCAL GATE SECURITY AND CAAA DELIVERY PROTOCOLS Delivery Address: CAAA, 300 Highway 361, Crane, IN 47522. Receiving Hours: 0700 to 1430, Monday through Thursday (excluding Holidays). By Appointment Only: Deliveries require a Carrier Appointm

NAICS: 541310 Architectural Services (Sector: Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services). PSC: C1DA Architect and Engineering Construction: Hospitals and Infirmaries. The Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC), HSA 1.3 Contracting, 200 Veterans Drive, Beckley, WV 25801, is soliciting Architect/Engineer (A/E) Services to provide Schematic Design, Life Cycle Cost Analysis (LCCA), Design Development, Construction and Bid Documents, Specifications, Construction Cost Estimates, and construction period services for the Renovate Specialty Clinics on 2nd Floor project at the Beckley VAMC, 200 Veterans Drive, Beckley, WV 25801. Set Aside This acquisition is a 100% Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set aside. Any subsequent award will require firms to be: Registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov; Visible and certified in the SBA Veteran Small Business Certification database at https://search.certifications.sba.gov; Compliant with VETS 4212 reporting at https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212. Important Notice THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. This is a request for SF 330 Architect/Engineer Qualifications packages only. Submission Requirements This acquisition is for A/E Services and is procured in accordance with the Brooks Act as implemented in FAR Subpart 36.6. To be considered for this contract, firms shall submit SF 330s electronically as follows: Submit SF 330 Parts I and II by email to millard.adkins@va.gov as a single Adobe PDF file (no larger than 10 MB). No ZIP files. Receipt must be confirmed. SF 330s are due no later than 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on October 26, 2026. Your response shall follow the same order as the Evaluation Factors listed below. Failure to follow this format may result in rejection of the SF 330. The SF 330 form can be found on the GSA forms website at www.gsa.gov. All questions must be emailed to Millard.Adkins@va.gov no later than 2:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on October 14, 2026. Potential contractors must be registered in SAM (www.sam.gov), visible and certified in https://search.certifications.sba.gov, and compliant in VETS 4212 (https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/vets4212) at the time of submission and at the time of award. Include an insert with the following: SAM UEI, Tax Identification Number, the email address and phone number of the primary point of contact, and a printed copy of the firm s SDVOSB certification/registry. Offerors shall provide all documents listed and comply with all instructions for their proposal to be considered responsive. Unverified SDVOSBs will be considered nonresponsive and will not be evaluated. General Information This is a Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business set aside. NAICS 541310; size standard $12.5 million. No solicitation package or bidder/plan holder list will be issued, and no solicitation documents are available. This procurement is subject to the availability of funds. The Government is under no obligation to award a contract because of this announcement. A/E Eligibility and Disciplines The selected A/E firm shall meet the FAR 2.101 definition of Architect engineer services as defined in 40 U.S.C. 1102 and FAR 36.6. The SDVOSB architectural firm must employ the principal Architect responsible for the design of this project and be heavily involved in all aspects of the design, including stamping drawings along with other team disciplines. A/Es signing drawings must be licensed; licenses are required at the time of award. Disciplines expected to be required: Architecture; Structural; Civil; Mechanical (HVAC); Plumbing; Electrical; Fire Protection; Industrial Hygiene; Interior Design; Surveying; Cost Estimating; Certified Physical Security Specialist; and other A/E services as defined by FAR 36.6 as necessary. Project Identification Renovate Specialty Clinics on 2nd Floor Project No. 517 22 202 A/E SCOPE OF WORK GENERAL: This project, Non-recurring Maintenance, will engage an architectural/engineering (A/E) firm to provide a complete design for a new renovation of our 2nd floor specialty and support space to create updated clinic spaces. This project would provide much needed improvements at the VA Beckley Campus. This project will require extensive assistance from the A/E interior designer as this is an area that is viewed heavily by Veterans, family, visitors, and staff throughout the day to day while in the building. Our facility presently does not have an interior designer on staff. Therefore, this will require the A/E interior designer to be heavily engaged with the VA staff throughout the entire process to achieve an aesthetically pleasing appearance to the 2nd floor. Although the project is for approximately 16,530 square feet on the 2nd, an all-inclusive concept will need to be created. This will lay the groundwork to provide a world class care setting for this hospital. This project will help reinforce the quality of care that our Veterans receive. The A/E would be expected to collaborate with other A/E firms involved in other projects throughout the facility. The renovation is anticipated to be extensive due to the building s original construction dating back to the 1950 s. Given its age, significant upgrades to all systems are expected to be necessary to meet current code, standards, and VA requirements. PURPOSE: The desired result is to provide improvements for approximately 16,530 square feet of specialty clinic space, located on the 2nd floor of BECVAMC Building 1. The renovation will provide our veterans with an updated central check-in and waiting area, improved wayfinding through updated layout, and improved traffic flows. It will also improve the clinic layout as the current clinic space was originally designed for medical surgical care. The 2nd floor has approximately 58,853 square feet that must be evaluated to determine the optimum location and layout for clinic space. The existing conditions for specialty clinics are spread over many floors of the hospital with hopes to bring or relocate most/many to the 2nd floor. This project would allow our facility to utilize a one-stop care approach by bringing services directly to our Veterans in their exam rooms. By creating correctly sized exam rooms it will help to accommodate the Veterans, their family, and caregivers who accompany them to their appointments. The design would also accommodate Veterans who use mobility scooters and larger wheelchairs. Veteran privacy will be enhanced by reducing foot and equipment traffic This project will renovate to provide space to meet VA guidelines. This project would establish a central check-in and waiting area for the 2nd floor clinics that would be easily accessible and accommodate Veterans and their caregivers. The waiting area would also improve efficiency and wayfinding, as well as increase Veteran satisfaction. LOCATION: Building 1, primarily on the 2nd floor of the VA Medical Center in Beckley, WV. PROJECT: This project includes but is not limited to the items listed below. The architect shall produce construction drawings for a full design encompassing all disciplines. Such as demolition and new construction, interiors, phasing plans for work, infection control plans, outages, mechanical and temporary access during construction, as well as furniture, fixtures, and equipment. VA Beckley has been approved for the renovation of the 2nd floor area and support space to create, expand clinics that will comply with VA guidelines. The architect shall verify and detail all utility moves and upgrades to support the renovation floorplans. description: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project at the Coatesville VA Medical Center � located in Coatesville, PA. All installed cables shall be terminated at each end and documentation, labeling, and (where applicable) test results provided. This applies to all permanently installed cable types. All Copper replacement will be CAT 6A. CAT 6A Patch Cords shall be provided and installed for all locations, including patch cords at the End User Device and at the TR. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YRBM-50
description: 14 October 2026- Reason for Amendment 0002 is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. Also, the Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachment 6 References and Drawings have been updated as of 13 October 2026. ________________________________ 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L. ________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. This is a 100% Small Business set-aside under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 336611, size standard 1,300 employees. All offerors must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) to receive award of Government contracts. Offerors are advised also that SAM representations and certifications can be completed electronically via the System for Award Management website at https://www.sam.gov.

title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YRBM-50
description: October 14 2026- Reason for Amendment 0002 is to extend the RFC due date from 8 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 15 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT and the proposal due date from 19 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT to 26 October 2026 at 12:00 PM PT. Also, the Attachment 1 Statement of Work and Attachment 6 References and Drawings have been updated as of 13 October 2026. ________________________________ 17 September 2026- Reason for amendment 0001 is to add additional ship check date, extend the deadline for clarifications and solicitation end date. See section L. ________________________________ The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS and IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish maintenance, repair, and preservation of YRBM-50. The YRBM-50 characteristics are Length: 153FT, Width: 43FT, Age: 82 Years, Hull Type: Steel, Draft: 6FT, Full Displacement: 900 L Tons and Light Load: 427 L Tons. The Contractors facility must possess the capability of YRBM-50 with the dimensions as stated above. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the SUPERVISOR to deliver the vessel to the Contractors facility. To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility where the work will be performed shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the west of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. Upon docking vessel, wash, and clean vessel. Accomplish required inspections and fender repairs. Remove existing and install new zinc anodes. Hull, freeboard and exterior decks require ultrasonic measurement of plating thickness and repair of areas below minimum thickness as needed. Accomplish blast and paint preservation of hull, freeboard, exterior decks and superstructure. Vessel requires inspection for damage and deterioration (hull, exterior decks, and tanks/voids plating and framing). Apply new non-skid system to exterior decks. Open, clean, ventilate, inspect, test, and maintain dry each tank/void. Accomplish partial preservation of QTY (24 EA) ballast tanks/voids. Accomplish access cover and watertight hatch and door repairs. Disinfect and certify potable water system. Pump and clean the interior surfaces of the CHT tank. Accomplish main deck repairs, hawse hole bulls eye and bolster repairs, and hull fendering system modifications. Accomplish the following modifications: hot water heater installation, awning replacement, A/C plant replacement and backup systems, switchboard upgrades, 1MC replacement and phone system upgrades, and CCTV upgrades. Undock the vessel. Verify vessel drawings and provide redline drawings to reflect actual conditions of the vessel. Conduct dock trials. Coordinate with the SUPERVISOR to support and accomplish all contract requirements prior to the availability end date. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the SUPERVISOR. Specific details of all work items and tasks required by the Statement of Work described in this Scope Overview are included in Section 3.0 of the Statement of Work. The vessel availability is scheduled to be 31 March 2027 through 31 March 2028. title: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1
description: Sources Sought/Request for Information Upper Mississippi River Restoration (UMRR) � Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project- Stage 1 Purpose and Objectives: The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding: (1) the availability and capability of all qualified companies; (2) whether they are small or large businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran- owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their understanding and experience relative to the proposed acquisition to assist the Government in determining the expectation of receiving bids from responsible contractors at fair market prices. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set- aside is possible. An organization that is not under the applicable NAICS code can submit a response to this notice, however their capabilities may/may not be assessed for the purposes of this notice. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement as a set-aside based upon responses to this Notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Corps of Engineers (COE), Rock Island District does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses received. This announcement is for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as commitment by the Government, implied or otherwise, to issue a solicitation or make a contract award. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. This is NOT a request for proposal, quote or invitation for bid. Interested parties are expected to review this Notice and the Project Requirements to familiarize themselves with the requirements of this project. NAICS Code and Size Standard: In the event a solicitation is issued, North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a size standard of $45 Million, is being considered. Solicitation Type: The Government is considering using a RFO FAR 14 Invitation for Bid for solicitation of this project. Background: The Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project area spans approximately 2,350 acres along the right descending bank of the Upper Mississippi River System, situated between River Mile 327.0 to 332.0 within Pool 21. It is located in Adams County, Illinois adjacent to the City of Quincy. The project area contains several Mississippi River Project Master Plan land classifications, including Wildlife Management, High Density Recreation, and Vegetation Management land classifications. Historically, Quincy Bay was an important stopover point for diving ducks during spring and fall migrations. Sedimentation within the project area has resulted in decreased water depths and reduced habitat availability. Today, the reduced depth of the Upper Bay and lack of aquatic vegetation supports very few migratory waterfowl. Furthermore, floodplain forests have experienced an increase in invasive species and a decrease in regeneration and diversity. Relatively diverse pre-settlement floodplain forests are now largely dominated by silver maple and cottonwood. Without restoration, the project area�s open waters would continue to convert to shallow backwaters and drier bottomland forests would continue to develop into plant communities dominated by flood tolerant species and invasive species such as reed canary grass and Japanese hops. The entirety of the Quincy Bay Habitat Rehabilitation and Enhancement Project consists of the following proposed activities and features: dredged material placement with forest rehabilitation, dredging for overwintering habitat and sediment reduction, bank stabilization, river training structures, cut-through channel modification, Cedar Creek modification, vegetated overflow structures, aquatic vegetation plantings, timber stand improvement, and pothole enhancement. The total project will be carried out in multiple stages. The focus of this Sources Sought is Stage 1: dredging for overwintering habitat, access dredging, topographic diversity enhancement, bank stabilization, and river training structures. Project Requirements: Stage 1: Dredging for Overwintering Habitat (OW 1-3), Access Dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), Topographic Diversity (TD 1-4), Bank Stabilization (BS 2), and River Training Structure (RTS 4-5) See Figure 1 for feature locations. Areas considered as part of this Project and described as the Project area include Quincy Bay, Quinsippi Island, backwater areas, and adjacent federally owned General Plan Lands. Approximately 16 acres of Quincy Bay and backwater channels will require access dredging (AD-OW-1 AD-OW-3), with approximately 19 acres requiring additional dredging to create deeper overwintering habitat (OW 1-3) for native species. Mechanical excavation/dredging will be required. Channel depths are up to 8 feet below flat pool and will have a channel bottom between 50 and 60 feet wide. Quantities excavated will be approximately 260,000 cubic yards of material over a total length approaching 16,000 feet. Excavated material will be side cast where possible and shaped to tie into the existing bankline. This material will be handled multiple times. Side casting will only be possible for a portion of the material to be removed from the dredge cuts. Material that cannot be side cast and shaped will need to be hauled to the shoreline placement sites. Placement sites are located at a minimum of 25 feet from the channel cut. The placement sites vary in width ranging from approximately 40 feet wide to 60 feet wide. Material will be required to remain within the placement site limits, with no material allowed to reenter the channel cuts, or be removed from the project area. These dredge placement sites will be used for topographic diversity features (TD 1-4). A top elevation may not be exceeded at the placement sites, and material will be required to be spread evenly across the placement sites in preparation for future work. Shaping of these sites to maintain a side slope will also be required. Tree/brush clearing will be required in select locations to ensure placement sites tie into the bankline. Trees outside of the placement site limits will not be damaged or removed. Bank stabilization (BS 2) for approximately 400 linear feet on Cedar Creek will require clearing; hauling, grading, and shaping; and placement of 1,100 tons of RR3 sized stone, with approximately 8 inches of bedding stone underlay. The bank will be shaped to maintain a predetermined slope to height ratio per the project design, with consideration for the width of the stone placement. Surveying after the bank stabilization to confirm the appropriate ratio will be required. River Training Structures (RTS 4-5) along the exterior edge of topographic diversity placement (TD1) will require specific shaping of dredged material to create more diversity in the placement alignment/orientation. This will be a construction contract to be primarily constructed during 2028. Capability Statement/Information Sought: All parties interested in this project must demonstrate that they would have the potential to be a responsive and responsible contractor. Interested businesses shall include the following information to be considered for this Sources Sought announcement: Company Name, UEI/CAGE (If your company does not have at the time of this sources sought, please be aware that you will be required to register your company in the System of Award Management (SAM) system to be eligible for any future Federal contracts), POC information including an email, current small business and socio-economic status for the NAICS code listed above. If excavation interferes with existing drains, piping, or structures, the Contractor shall immediately notify, in writing, the COR and provide temporary protection for these systems before proceeding. Trenching from Handholes The Contractor shall make wall penetrations into existing manholes/handholes as required for the number and size of conduits entering and exiting each structure, in accordance with the drawings. Conduit Existing conduit shall remain in place unless the drawings specifically direct removal or modification. Under grass, soil, the Contractor shall install Schedule 80 PVC conduit with a minimum cover of 24 inches (610 mm) from finished grade to top of conduit, or as indicated on the drawings, whichever is greater. All underground 90 degree bends with a 12inch (305 mm) radius shall use prefabricated sweeping bends. Above grade, all underground PVC conduit shall transition to rigid galvanized steel (RGS) using PVC to RGS couplers. The Contractor shall install pull lines in all new conduit runs. Soil and Backfill Materials Soil Materials The Contractor shall provide all labor and materials for soil and backfill, where required. Select Backfill: ASTM D 2487 soil classification groups SW, SP, and SM, or combinations thereof; free of rock or gravel larger than 3 inches (75 mm), debris, waste, frozen materials, vegetation, and other deleterious matter. Asphalt/Concrete Base Course: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; with at least 95% passing a 11/2inch (40 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Base Gravel: Naturally or artificially graded mixture of natural or crushed gravel, crushed stone, and natural or crushed sand; ASTM D 2940; 100% passing a 1inch (25 mm) sieve and not more than 8% passing a 1/4inch (6.4 mm) sieve. Sand Cushion: ASTM C 33 fine aggregate, natural or manufactured sand. Placement and Compaction Place backfill and fill in layers not exceeding: 8 inches (203 mm) loose thickness for heavy compaction equipment; 4 inches (102 mm) loose thickness when compacted by hand-operated tampers. Place backfill and fill evenly to the required elevations, uniformly along their full length. Compact soil materials to not less than the following percentages of maximum dry unit weight per ASTM D 1557: Under lawns or unpaved areas: scarify and re-compact top 6 inches (152 mm) below subgrade and compact each layer to 85%. title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed above. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed above. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources. Update as of 10/1/26 Submission Format Requirements Use Times New Roman, 12?point font for all text. Maintain 1?inch margins on all sides of every page. The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30?page limit. Please do not paginate these two sections. Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats. Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov. In the email subject line, format the title exactly as: �Response to GSMO?4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]� Scope Guidance NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research. If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate �Limited Scope� on the Cover Page, along with a brief description of the capabilities included. Q&A Sessions The program intends to hold formal one?on?one Q&A sessions with vendors once the RFI period closes. Dates and duration for these sessions are TBD.
