title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources. Update as of 10/1/26 Submission Format Requirements Use Times New Roman, 12?point font for all text. Maintain 1?inch margins on all sides of every page. The Cover Page and Table of Contents do not count toward the 30?page limit. Please do not paginate these two sections. Submit your response in both PDF and Word (.docx) formats. Email all submissions directly to daniel.s.han@nasa.gov. In the email subject line, format the title exactly as: �Response to GSMO?4 RFI [Company Name, CAGE Code]� Scope Guidance NASA welcomes submissions that provide limited scope information for internal market research. If your response covers only a portion of the contract scope, please clearly indicate �Limited Scope� on the Cover Page, along with a brief description of the capabilities included. Q&A Sessions The program intends to hold formal one?on?one Q&A sessions with vendors capable of delivering the full contract scope once the RFI period closes. Dates and duration for these sessions are TBD.

description: Amendment 0001 is hereby posted. ________________________________________________________________________ The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. title: Construction Services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage St. Elizabeths West Campus
description: The General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service (PBS), is seeking a qualified contractor for construction services for the Gate 7 Parking Garage at the St. Elizabeths West Campus in Southeast Washington, DC. GSA anticipates awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price construction contract for the new construction of the Gate 7 Parking Garage and associated site, utility, security, stormwater, landscape, and infrastructure improvements. The project will support the operational needs of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) at the St. Elizabeths West Campus. This acquisition is for construction services only. The project design is being completed separately by GSA�s Architect of Record, ZGF. The construction solicitation is based on Issued for Construction drawings, specifications, and related contract documents. The work to be performed under the terms of this contract includes, but is not limited to, furnishing all management, supervision, subcontractors, labor, materials, supplies, tools, equipment, coordination, quality control, testing, inspections, commissioning support, and closeout documentation necessary to construct the Gate 7 Parking Garage in accordance with the contract documents. The project includes construction of a new multi-level parking garage with associated surface parking, access and screening infrastructure, and related campus improvements. The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Site development, clearing, grading, excavation, and civil infrastructure improvements Utility relocations, extensions, tie-ins, and connections Substructure construction, including foundations, slab-on-grade, excavation support, waterproofing, and retaining walls Parking garage structure, including structural framing, parking decks, ramps, stairs, elevators, roof assemblies, and related structural components Mechanically ventilated parking garage systems, including ventilation equipment, shafts, ductwork, louvers or openings, controls, electrical power, life-safety interfaces, testing, balancing, and commissioning support Exterior fa�ade and building envelope construction, including a classical architectural brick fa�ade with openings Exterior doors, windows, louvers, waterproofing, sealants, flashings, and related envelope components Mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire protection, fire alarm, emergency communications, lighting, controls, IT, telecommunications, electronic security, access control, CCTV, parking guidance, and related systems Physical security elements, including vehicle barriers, bollards, gates, credentialing areas, and screening-related infrastructure Roadway, shuttle, pedestrian circulation, hardscape, landscape, site lighting, signage, and related site improvements Stormwater management facilities, erosion and sediment control, and environmental protection measures Testing, inspections, commissioning support, training, warranties, as-built documentation, BIM/COBie deliverables where applicable, and project closeout The Gate 7 Parking Garage will be constructed within the active St. Elizabeths West Campus, a high-security federal campus and National Historic Landmark. The contractor will be required to coordinate construction activities with ongoing campus operations, security requirements, occupied facilities, existing utilities, shuttle operations, adjacent work, traffic and access impacts, and protection of historic and environmental resources. The contractor may also be required to coordinate with District of Columbia agencies or authorities, as applicable, for traffic control, haul routes, public space, utility, roadway, permit, or other construction-related requirements. All work shall conform to applicable GSA requirements, the 2026 PBS Core Building Standards, contract drawings and specifications, campus security requirements, applicable codes and standards, and project-specific requirements. The estimated cost range for construction is between $120,000,000.00 and $160,000,000.00. The intended project delivery method is a Phased Acquisition procurement using a Two-Phase Construction Concept. Specific security requirements will be contained in the solicitation. FUNDS AVAILABILITY: Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. Potential offerors are responsible for monitoring and downloading the solicitation and any potential amendments, if any, to the solicitation.

title: Ground Systems and Mission Operations-4 (GSMO-4)
description: This RFI is for informational purposes only. It is not a request for proposals or a solicitation for a contract or grant award and it does not obligate the Government in any way. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with responding to this request. Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is seeking information from qualified vendors capable of supporting science and Earth science missions including, but not limited to: Earth Observing System; Earth Observing System Data and Operations System; Magnetospheric Multi-Scale mission; Global Precipitation Measurement mission; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter; James Webb Space Telescope; Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope; Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (built by NASA for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration); Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope; and Solar Dynamics Observatory. This RFI is intended to gather market intelligence, technical approaches, and rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) considerations to inform a potential future procurement. Background The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) currently acquires mission operations support through the Goddard Space Mission Operations (GSMO?3) contract. GSMO?3 provides comprehensive, end?to?end mission operations services spanning the entire mission life cycle. The scope of work includes systems and facility engineering; launch and early?orbit operations support; flight operations and flight dynamics services; sustaining engineering; and mission operations studies, design, integration, and testing of ground systems. Additional services include mission data collection and distribution, system administration, and information technology security and engineering analyses. The GSMO?3 contract supports a broad portfolio of NASA science and Earth science missions, including the Earth Observing System (EOS), Magnetospheric Multi?Scale (MMS), Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM), Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Fermi Gamma?ray Space Telescope, Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES), Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). These services are essential to sustaining and advancing NASA�s ground data systems and mission operations infrastructure, ensuring reliable communication, data processing, and mission control capabilities for ongoing and future missions. The contract also supports mission decommissioning and long?term sustaining engineering required to maintain operational readiness for systems with multidecade lifespans. The scope also increasingly encompasses cloud infrastructure management, continuous cybersecurity monitoring, DevSecOps automation, and advanced collision avoidance/conjunction assessment activities. Functions FUNCTION 1- Mission Ground System Support Services A. Ground Systems Engineering and Engineering Studies B. Ground Systems Support Services C. Ground Systems Integration and Test Services FUNCTION 2 - Mission Operations System Support Services A. Operations Systems Engineering B. Launch and Early Operations Support C. Flight Operations D. Flight Dynamics Support Services E. Mission Data Collection and Distribution F. Mission Systems Sustaining Engineering G. Systems Administration and IT Security H. Database Administration RFI Response Instructions The Government is seeking feedback from contractors with relevant mission capabilities and experience. Responses should include the vendor implementation approach and rough order magnitude costs of performing the functions listed below. Responses should be limited to no more than 30 pages. Transition from Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) to Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) The Government is evaluating the feasibility of transitioning the follow-on GSMO-4 requirement from a Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contract to a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract, either in whole or in part, including the use of Performance Based Payments for FFP Tasks. The Government seeks industry feedback regarding the practicality of such an approach. Specifically, respondents are requested to address the following: Is the current GSMO-4 scope sufficiently defined and stable to support an FFP contract? If not, identify the areas of uncertainty. What technical, programmatic, schedule, or cost risks would your organization associate with transitioning this requirement from CPAF to FFP? Which portions of the requirement, if any, do you believe are well-suited for FFP, and which portions would be more appropriately performed under another contract type (e.g., Time-and-Materials)? Please explain your rationale. What assumptions or Government-provided information (e.g., historical workload, staffing profiles, performance metrics, technical baseline, service level agreements, demand forecasts, configuration data) would be necessary for your organization to develop a realistic fixed-price proposal? What contract incentives or performance metrics would improve the viability of an FFP approach? What acquisition or contract structure would best balance cost control, performance, innovation, and risk allocation for this requirement? Please identify any lessons learned or best practices from similar transitions from Cost-Reimbursement to Firm-Fixed-Price contracts. Are there specific contract provisions or performance requirements that should be modified to enable a successful transition to FFP? Catalog Pricing Structure: The Government is exploring a 'Catalog-style' pricing structure for routine Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) operations, where missions are priced based on their Risk Classification (e.g., Class B, C, D). What are the benefits, risks, and potential cost-drivers your firm would associate with pricing mission operations by Class? What specific parameters, boundaries, or Service Level Agreements (SLAs) would be required in the catalog definitions to make this pricing model viable. Core vs. IDIQ Structure: The Government is considering a contract structure that establishes highly stable, long-term flagship missions as the baseline 'Core' requirement, with all other missions and development efforts issued as IDIQ task orders. How would this Core-plus-IDIQ structure impact your pricing, workforce retention, and risk allocation strategies compared to a 100% IDIQ structure. Requirements/Specifications Available Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Resources: The Government maintains operations resources listed below. RFI responses may include the use of these GFE resources. For any GFE resources incorporated in their response, the vendor should include any GSMO implementation costs and the cost differences/savings as compared to the vendor providing all ground resources.

title: PA161/PA103A2 Metal Containers for the 155mm Modular Artillery Charge System (MACS) M231/232
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Rock Island (RI) at Picatinny, in support of the Office of the Project Manager Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), has a requirement for the production of PA161/PA103A2 Metal Containers in support of the 155mm Modular Artillery Charge System (MACS) M231/M232 and variants. This effort is for a new 5-year sole-source Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity contract with Firm-Fixed-Price delivery orders to support FY2027-31 requirements. This action is a follow-on contract for the continued production of PA161/PA103A2 Metal Containers. The new sole-source award will be made to Conco, Inc. located in Louisville, KY on an other than full and open competition basis utilizing Title 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 3204(a)(3) as implemented by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-3 (Industrial Mobilization; Engineering, Developmental, or Research Capability; or Expert Services). Award is projected for 3rd Qtr FY27. In accordance with RFO 16.504-1(b), the contract will include a minimum guarantee in the amount of $5.2 million. The estimated maximum contract value for this new effort is $586M. The production quantities over the 5 years would be as follows: PA161 Metal Containers: 920,145 and PA103A2 Metal Containers: 3,090,060. The PA161/PA103A2 containers are currently produced by Conco, Inc. The PA161 and PA103A2 Metal Containers are square-rimmed 6-inch diameter cylindrical steel shipping and storage containers between 31 and 38 inches in length and used for the 155mm M231 and M232 MACS. Two different propelling charges of the 155mm M231 and M232-series provide a complete zoning solution for 155mm artillery applications by using multiples of basic increment. The M231 charges are used at lower zones (Zones 1 and 2), while M232-series charges are used at progressively higher zones. A total of four M231 MACS are packed per PA161 container, while five M232A2 MACS are packed per PA103A2 container. These containers were developed to protect the MACS charges throughout the Army's stringent logistic environments and have design features that improve the insensitive munitions characteristics for the MACS system. Level III Government-Owned Technical Data Packages (TDPs) are available for the PA161 and PA103A2 Metal Containers and will be used for this requirement. The TDPs are coded as Distribution Statement D (authorized distribution of technical documents to the Department of War (DoW) and U.S. DoW Contractors only). A fully executed DD Form 2345 and a completed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) will be required prior to receiving the TDPs. The point of contact for the TDP request will be Ms. Giuliana Turriciano, giuliana.turriciano.civ@army.mil. This is a Pre-Solicitation notice, and the Government anticipates release of the Request for Proposal (RFP) in December 2026. Any information or exchanges between contractors and the Government concerning this notice are at no additional cost and/or obligation to the Government. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this effort is 332439. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database by accessing the SAM website at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for contract award. This notice does not constitute a formal RFP, nor is the Government obligated to issue an RFP. However, interested sources may submit a capability statement demonstrating their firm's technical ability of this requirement. All inquiries shall be made via e-mail only. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. The point of contacts for this requirement are the Procurement Officer via renee.k.prendergast.civ@army.mil AND the Contract Specialist at giuliana.turriciano.civ@army.mil.

STATUTORY & REGULATORY AUTHORITY: Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support (DLAWS), Industrial Plant Equipment Services Division (VICA), intends to award a Sole-Source, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements) and FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(ii) (substantial duplication of cost not expected to be recovered through competition), in conjunction with FAR Part 12 (Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services). 2. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION & TECHNICAL QUALITY STANDARDS: � Item Description: One (1) DN PUMA Vertical Turning Center (VTC) 1620M Machine � Scope: Turnkey delivery, rigging, installation, on-site calibration, and operational testing in strict accordance with Purchase Description VIBB 26-26-1001, dated 05 May 2026. � Delivery Period: 355 calendar days After Receipt of Order (ARO), followed by thirty (30) calendar days for Government final acceptance testing. � Condition: All items delivered shall be in New (unused) condition; Government surplus, refurbished, and prototype items are strictly prohibited. Non-National Stock Number (Non-NSN) item. Alternate offers will not be considered. � Delivery Location: Trident Refit Facility (TRF) Bangor, Naval Base Kitsap, Silverdale, WA (FOB Destination). 3. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROVISION (QAP) 175a: Quality Assurance Provision (QAP) 175a applies to this procurement. In accordance with QAP 175a: � Calibration Standards: All Contractor inspection, measurement, and test equipment (M&TE) utilized in determining conformity of supplies with contract requirements shall maintain a current, valid calibration traceable to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). � Final Inspection Notification: The Contractor shall provide DLA Weapons Support with at least fifteen (15) business days of advance written notification from the date the item(s) will be fully installed, operational, and ready for final inspection and acceptance at destination. � Quality Discrepancy / Delay Notification: If the item(s) fail the Contractor�s on-site quality checks and will not be ready for Government inspection as originally scheduled, the Contractor shall provide advance written notice to DLA Weapons Support at least three (3) business days prior to the established inspection date. 4. STREAMLINED COMBINED NOTICE: Pursuant to FAR 12.202(b) and FAR 12.603, this notice combines the pre-solicitation synopsis and the Request for Quotes (RFQ) to streamline procurement timeframes for acquisitions exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT). 5. ORGANIZED SITE VISIT & INQUIRIES: An organized site visit is scheduled for Tuesday, September 29, 2026, at 08:30 AM Pacific Time (PT) at TRF Bangor, Building 7000, Naval Base Kitsap � Bangor. Mandatory base pre-registration and SECNAV Form 5512/1 submissions must be completed no later than seven (7) business days prior to the visit. Full instructions are set forth in the RFQ package. 6. POINT OF CONTACT: Christina Gibbs, Contract Specialist Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support (DLAWS) - VICA Defense Supply Center Richmond (DSCR) Email: christina.gibbs@dla.mil

title: Notice of Intent Sole Source Audio/Visual Services at the Washington Hilton
description: This is a Notice of Intent to Award a Soel Source Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract using FAR Part 12 and FAR Part 13 procedures. Service needed: Audio and visual services at the Washington Hilton for the Marine Corps Ball. See Document "JnA REDACTED" for detail. The government intends to award on a Sole Source basis to: Dupont Hotel Project Owner, LLC, 1919 Connecticut AVE NW Washington, District of Columbia, 20009, United States. The circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available. The basis for this Sole Source Award Intent is that the hotel is the only entity through which the required audio-visual services for the Marine Corps Ball at the designated Hilton venue can be procured in accordance with applicable contracting and payment requirements. The venue's exclusive arrangement with its licensed audio-visual service provider necessitates that the services be secured through the hotel. Interested vendors: vendors interested in obtaining the same capability may respond via email to receive Marine Corps System Command's point of contact. In our response, please indicate whether you can provide the required services at the specified location. Responses by no later than 26 October, 2026, 4:00 PM EST.

Submissions must include datasheets, drawings, or specifications that demonstrate compliance with performance requirements outlined in the technical description. Any deviation from the stated technical requirements must be clearly identified and justified. 5. Certification and Traceability Vendors must certify that all components are new, unused, and conform to commercial standards. Traceability documentation shall be provided to verify the supply chain from the original manufacturer to the vendor. Documentation may include FAA Form 8130-3, Certificate of Conformance, Part Manufacturer Approval (PMA) Documentation or equivalent. Authorized Release Certificate Requirement ? For new (spare) components, the 8130-3 shall be issued by an FAA-approved production approval holder (PAH) and certify that the item conforms to FAA- approved design data and is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). Delivery and Packaging Items shall be packaged in accordance with standard commercial practices that prevent damage during transit and storage unless otherwise specified. All shipments must be traceable and include packing lists identifying part number, nomenclature, quantity, and contract number. 7. Warranty and Support A standard commercial warranty must be provided. Warranty terms must be at least equal to those provided to the vendor?s commercial customers and must include workmanship and replacement parts. Technical support must be available during the warranty period. 8. Marking and Labeling Components must be labeled with the part number, manufacturer's name or CAGE code, and lot or serial number (if applicable). 9. Traceability documentation shall be provided to verify the supply chain from the original manufacturer to the vendor. For new (spare) components, the 8130-3 shall be issued by an FAA-approved production approval holder (PAH) and certify that the item conforms to FAA- approved design data and is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor

title: R--Technical Support for Drinking Water Optimization Program
description: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is performing a market search to determine potential capable sources in preparation for a future procurement. Information submitted in response to this notice is for internal market research purposes and no feedback will be offered to the interested parties that submit capability statements. For background, the subject acquisition is anticipated to provide support services for the �Technical Support for the Drinking Water Optimization Program.� The drinking water optimization program began in the late 1980�s with a focus on enhancement and implementation of the Drinking Water Composite Correction Program (CCP). Implementation of the CCP resulted in documented improvements on individual surface water treatment plant performance. The documented success of the CCP, its value for drinking water primacy programs and the desire to apply CCP principles more broadly resulted in the creation of an Area-wide Optimization Program (AWOP). Broad-scale public water system performance improvements and the resulting drinking water quality improvements have been achieved via AWOP implementation. Public Water System Supervision (PWSS) programs implement their AWOPs to enhance public health protection and to benefit from the resulting proactive assistance with regulatory compliance. The AWOP was established with a focus on turbidity removal, resulting in greater protection against the risk of microbial pathogens passing through treatment plant processes. The program continues the focus on turbidity removal while expanding its technical scope to include optimization of both treatment plant and distribution system operations to minimize the formation of disinfection by-products (DBPs) and maintaining adequate disinfectant residual. The technical scope of the program also includes optimization of process control for ground water treatment and conveyance, and many unconventional (alternate) treatment processes. The program�s documented impact on enhancing public health protection has also been called upon to address other public health challenges such as treatment for cyanobacteria associated with harmful algal blooms and arsenic removal. The National AWOP has been structured to address additional public health challenges, depending on the commitment of resources to the program. For more information, please see the attached Sources Sought Notification and Draft Performance Work Statement.

Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR Part 13/15, as applicable (based on dollar value or acquisition method) DFARS 212, as applicable for Department of Defense requirements 3. Commercial Item Determination: Offerors shall provide documentation Supporting the commerciality of the offered item(s), which may include: Commercial product descriptions and technical specifications Sales history or catalog pricing Copies of sales invoices or redacted purchase orders to non-government Customers published price lists or marketing materials 4. Technical Requirements Offered components must meet the Government's form, fit, and function requirements. Submissions must include datasheets, drawings, or specifications that demonstrate compliance with performance requirements outlined in the technical description. Any deviation from the stated technical requirements must be clearly identified and justified. 5. Certification and Traceability Vendors must certify that all components are new, unused, and conform to commercial standards. Traceability documentation shall be provided to verify the supply chain from the original manufacturer to the vendor. Documentation may include FAA Form 8130-3, Certificate of Conformance, Part Manufacturer Approval (PMA) Documentation or equivalent. Authorized Release Certificate Requirement ? FAA Form 8130-3 All components delivered under this contract shall be accompanied by a properly executed FAA Form 8130-3 Authorized Release Certificate. For new (spare) components, the 8130-3 shall be issued by an FAA-approved production approval holder (PAH) and certify that the item conforms to FAA- approved design data and is in a condition for safe operation (Block 11a). The 8130-3 must: Include the correct part number, serial number (if applicable), and contract/purchase order number and Be completed legibly and in accordance with current FAA guidance (e.g., FAA Order 8130.21 series) 6. Delivery and Packaging Items shall be packaged in accordance with standard commercial practices that prevent damage during transit and storage unless otherwise specified. All shipments must be traceable and include packing lists identifying part number, nomenclature, quantity, and contract number. 7. Warranty and Support A standard commercial warranty must be provided. Warranty terms must be at least equal to those provided to the vendor?s commercial customers and must include workmanship and replacement parts. Technical support must be available during the warranty period. 8. Marking and Labeling Components must be labeled with the part number, manufacturer's name or CAGE code, and lot or serial number (if applicable). 9. Contract Data Requirements No military-unique Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) will apply unless explicitly identified. Commercial documentation shall suffice unless otherwise negotiated. Can only be procured only from suppliers who provide FAA-Certified parts which possess a FAA Authorized Release Certificate, FAA Form 8130-3 Airworthy Approval Tag. For items for which Government inspection and acceptance will be conducted at the source, DLAD clause 52.?-9004, Product Verification Testing, is incorporated by reference. DLAD clauses can be viewed at http://www.dla.mil/Acquisition/Pages/DLAD.aspx. As applicable, DFARS clause 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, is incorporated by reference. Drawings are not available for this Request For Quote. Offerors are advised that offers received from sources which are not government-approved sources of supply will be deemed technically unacceptable, and therefore ineligible for award. Any distributors of approved sources MUST submit a copy of their authorized distributor letter, on the source letterhead, to the buyer point of contact indicated on the solicitation via email, at time of proposal submittal. All potential offers shall provide newly manufactured spares only. Refurbished, remanufactured, or repaired material will not be acceptable. Offers for such are ineligible for award. \

title: Transportation Security Administration (TSA) Industry Day: Horizon 25 OrchestrateSI and TalentSI
description: Industry Day Notice: FY2027 Transportation Security Administration (TSA) Industry Day: Horizon 25 OrchestrateSI and TalentSI The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) will host an Industry Day to engage industry partners on technology evolution efforts under the Horizon 25 Strategy: an integrated airport-operations capability and talent acquisition. The event will take place on October 20, 2026, from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM at TSA Headquarters in Springfield, Virginia. A virtual option will be available for registered participants unable to attend in person. TSA is working to strengthen security, elevate travelers� experience, improve checkpoint efficiency, and improve mission-support operations. TSA welcomes both traditional and non-traditional partners with agile, scalable, and mature solutions. Through this effort, TSA seeks practical technologies that can help the agency move from reactive processes to proactive, data-driven operations. Questions and suggestions may be submitted before or after the Industry Day to Horizon25.Industry@tsa.dhs.gov. TSA may consolidate and publicly post Government responses through an appropriate official channel. This Industry Day is for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation, commitment, or authorization for the Government to pay for information submitted. Registration Instructions If you are interested in attending, please RSVP by October 16, 2026 to Horizon25.Industry@tsa.dhs.gov with �TSA Horizon 25: OrchestrateSI and TalentSI Industry Day RSVP� in the subject line. Attendance is limited to those who RSVP by the deadline. Please provide the following information in your RSVP: If you are planning to attend in person, please attach the following info in a password-protected document: First Name, Last Name, Company, Foreign National -Yes/No, Date of Birth (DOB) and SSN. A MS Teams Virtual Meeting invitation will be sent to all registered industry partners along with the full agenda for the event. Company Name Attendee Name(s) and Title(s) Primary Point of Contact, including email address and phone number Primary NAICS Code Product Service Code Intended attendance: in person or virtual Relevant engagement area(s): Workforce Orchestration and Optimization Checkpoint Visualization, Digital Twin, and Bottleneck Detection Real-Time Airport Wait Time and Queue Intelligence Talent SI Note: Interested parties may submit non-proprietary capability statements, technical questions, and recommendations concerning technical requirements, pricing structure, evaluation criteria, and procurement strategy with their RSVP or after the event. Submitted materials should identify the applicable engagement area(s). TSA welcomes industry input as it refines requirements and acquisition approaches for these modernization efforts. ********************************* Update October 20, 2026. Submission of Responses and Contact Information Any questions suggestions, capabilities or considerations from this Industry day shall be submitted via email no later than 12:00 PM local time (Springfield, VA) on October 26, 2026 to Horizon25.Industry@tsa.dhs.gov and TSAIL@tsa.dhs.gov. Questions not received by the closing date and time may not be considered or reviewed by TSA. Questions in support of this event may or may not be addressed. Responses shall be submitted electronically, in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format with standard margins, 8.5�x11� paper size, and minimum of 11-point font and 9-point font for tables. Review of Responses The Government will review interested party questions for market research purposes only. The Government does not intend to provide responses to submitted questions directly but will consider or incorporate responses into any future solicitation relating to these requirements. The Government reserves the right to arrange a technical information exchange, demonstration, or pilot program directly with interested parties following review of the questions. Disclaimer This Industry Day is solely for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract, nor do they affect a potential offeror's ability to respond to any future synopsis/solicitation, which may or may not follow or restrict the Government's eventual acquisition approach. The Government will not provide reimbursement for any information that may be submitted in response to this notice, and no basis for a claim against the Government shall arise from a response to this notice or Government use of any information provided. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Industry Day. ********************************* Update October 23, 2026. Any questions, comments, suggestions, or capability statements regarding this Industry Day and/or the associated Statements of Objectives (SOO) must be submitted via email no later than 12:00 PM local time (Springfield, VA) on October 26, 2026.

For purposes of this section, Return is defined as physical receipt of the F-condition asset at the contractor's facility as reflected in the Action Date entry in the Commercial Asset Visibility (CAV) system. In accordance with the CAV Statement of Work, the contractor is required to accurately report all transactions by the end of the fifth regular business day after receipt and Action Date entered in CAV must be dated to reflect the actual date of physical receipt. The Contractor must obtain final inspection and acceptance by the Government for all assets within the RTATs established in this contract. Required RTAT: 090 days after receipt of asset Throughput Constraint: Contractor must provide a throughput Constraint for Each NSN(s). Total assets to be repaired monthly after initial delivery commences X/month (contractor fill in #). A throughput of ##____ per month reflects no throughput constraint. Induction Expiration Date: 365 days after contract award date. Any asset received after this date in days is not authorized for repair without bi-lateral agreement between the Contractor and NAVSUP WSS Contracting Officer. Reconciliation: A reconciliation modification will be issued after final Inspection and acceptance of all assets inducted under this contract. The parties have agreed to a price (shown on the schedule page) for each unit at the negotiated RTAT. Such prices are based on the Contractor meeting the RTAT requirements described within the schedule page. If the Contractor does not meet the applicable RTAT requirement, consideration will be assessed and subject to negotiation. The term "contract" encompasses a contract, an order, or a project work order. 3.2.2 OVERHAUL: An overhauled part is one which has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary (by replacing or repairing all components which have been found to exceed limits established by the repair/overhaul manual) reassembled and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW and returned to a Ready for Issue (RFI) condition (Refer to contract schedule for items to be overhauled). 3.2.3 REPAIR: A repaired part is one which has been restored to a Ready for Issue(RFI) condition (by replacing or repairing those components found to be defective, broken, damaged or inoperative during the initial evaluation and troubleshooting phase) and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW (Refer to contract schedule for items to be repaired). 3.3 3.0 SCOPE 3.3.1 GENERAL. title: Combined Synopsis / Solicitation for a potential Supply Chain Management Contract for F108 Engine Support � Mission Analysis
description: This notice serves as DLA Weapon Support�s combined synopsis/solicitation as described in FAR 12.603, in accordance with FAR 5.201, and the approved J&A under authority of FAR 6.103-1 and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), for addition of KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis for the CFM56-2 Engine, F108 Model Updates, and an F108 Self-Locking Borescope Plug set certification. This effort is anticipated to be made as an addition to sole source Long Term Contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406 to CFM International Inc. (CFM), Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) code 58828. This is a FAR part 12 effort being added to the current contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406. KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis, F108 Model Updates, and Borescope certification support services for the United States Air Force (USAF) are being solicited to be added to contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406, awarded to CFM International Inc. CAGE 58828. Actual requirements for the additional scope will be negotiated and added to the basic contract. Individual requirements are certified as sole source to CFM and synopsized in accordance with FAR 5.201. DLA Weapons Support will issue a letter solicitation (RFP) to the sole source Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). If any non-OEM source is interested in providing the entire support for this effort, please notify the Contracting Officer prior to the combined synopsis/solicitation closing date. A copy of the letter of interest should be forwarded to the Contracting Officer identified herein. The Government may alter the acquisition strategy if it is in the best interest of the Government. In order to receive an award, the contractor must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). SAM registration is at https://www.sam.gov. It is anticipated that this requirement will be added as a separate line item to the current sole source CFM COI contract SPE4AX-25-D-9406. The data required to perform the necessary services is CFM�s proprietary and confidential commercial intellectual data and cannot be shared or provided by the Government. Only sources with access to the F108 series of engines performance information will be considered as a qualified source. The scope of work is as follows: 1. KC/RC/WC135 Mission Analysis for the CFM56-2 Engine � The contractor shall define the mission characteristics and all variants that the KC135, RC135 and WC135 aircraft fly. The contractor shall assess the validity of engine usage assumptions made during engine certification and, by extension, the Life Limited Part (LLP) Low Cycle Fatigue (LCF) limitations and maintenance intervals published by CFMI. Since 1985, the KC135, RC135 and WC135 have been operating with the CFM56-2 engines as powerplants. In that time there have been several efforts accomplished by CFMI to verify the flight characteristics of the mission established for these weapon systems. The last assessment was accomplished in 2015, for high pressure system components and drove some changes to LLP lives. Since it has been a significant amount of time since the last assessment, another mission analysis is recommended to determine if the flight characteristics have changed significantly to impact life limits and maintenance intervals. The contractor shall perform all necessary tasks required to complete an assessment as described above. Using flight data provided by the Air Force and pilot interviews taken by CFMI, analysis will be conducted to establish the mission characteristics and possible impact to cycle definition, LLP limits and maintenance intervals. Once the contractor has completed the needed analysis and evaluation of the current KC/RC/WC135 missions, they will submit findings and results through their internal review process. Successful review will then drive a report for the Air Force that defines the mission characteristics along with a comparative review of the Air Force�s current mission versus previous mission. These results will be provided in a report to the USAF for USAF review and assessment. 2. F108 Model Updates � The contractor shall update thermal, CAD and stress F108 part models to prepare for future use during lifing analysis, field investigations, design tasks or other program needs. Thermal and stress analyses may be required to support lifing analysis following mission analysis updates; thermal and stress analyses may also be required in the future to support new field investigations or hardware redesign tasks. Multiple variants may need to be analyzed. Current models were constructed utilizing legacy tools (Patran, PThermal, Flow Network Solver). These models need to be transitioned to the current production tool set by passing them through the model conversion and upgrade process. This will convert them to Next-Gen Thermal & Flow Simulator. Modifications may be necessary to facilitate this process and ensure that converted model results align with legacy results within acceptable tolerances. Once this process is deemed successful, then additional model variants may be constructed. Upon completion of this, thermal and stress analyses can be performed. The contractor shall provide a memorandum confirming successful model updates to the USAF for USAF review and assessment. 3. F108 Self-Locking Borescope Plug set certification � The contractor shall provide a full self-locking borescope plug certification with a service bulletin release that approves the self-locking borescope plug set with a new auto-locking feature, eliminating the need for safety wire. The service bulletin will approve this new design, for us on the CFM56-2B engine configuration (USAF ref F108). The US Air Force F108 engine fleet has experienced breakages of the borescope plugs which can lead to FOD damage and presents a challenging effort to remove the broken pieces. These breakages are manifested in the 3 borescope plugs located at the stage 7, stage 8 and stage 9 positions of the high pressure compressor. Along with the breakages of these 3 plugs, all borescope plugs require safety wire as a redundant feature to ensure the plugs are locked in place. This results in extensive and unnecessary mission downtime as well as maintenance time to complete the laborious task of applying safety wire to all the plugs. The new self-locking borescope plug set consists of 15 new borescope plug assemblies that incorporate a new self-locking feature, which eliminates the requirement for safety wire. The new plug design also employs a more robust design for the compressor plugs at stage 7, stage 8 and stage 9 which eliminates the cause of breakages. So, the new borescope plug set reduces maintenance time as it eliminates the need for safety wire and reduces failures with a stronger plug at the vulnerable areas. The contractor shall perform all necessary tasks required to achieve certification of the Self Locking borescope plug set used on the CFM56-2 engines (USAF F108) and release a service bulletin documenting the approved application of this borescope plug set for use on the CFM56-2 engine configuration. Both the Original Engine Manufacturer (OEM) and the Air Force have experience with this type of self-locking design. However, the experience is on engines that have a different mission profile and the parts in use are not borescope plugs. It is necessary to have the engine manufacturer perform all necessary reviews and analysis to verify and validate the application of the borescope plug set on the CFM56-2 engine fleet. The contractor will perform all necessary analysis on the proposed design as well as develop any testing identified as needed for validation of functional capability in the CFM56-2 engine configuration. Analysis tasks can include but are not limited to review of usage history on other engine fleets with similar parts, modeling, comparative assessment between the existing borescope plugs and the proposed new plugs as well as review of certification efforts on other OEM engine fleets. description: Draft AOI: Industry Questions and Comments The Government welcomes industry questions and comments regarding this Draft Area of Interest (AOI). For purposes of this market engagement, questions and comments will be treated differently, as described below. The Government intends to respond to questions received by 4:00 PM Central Daylight Time (CDT) on 26 October 2026, with a target of publishing responses by close of business on 28 October 2026. Questions and Government responses will be made available to all prospective respondents. Comments: Comments are industry observations, recommendations, suggested revisions, or other feedback offered for Government consideration that do not request a response. The Government will take comments received by 4:00 PM CDT on 26 October 2026 under advisement in developing the Final AOI. The Government will not individually respond to or publish industry comments. Submissions After the Deadline: The Government will review and contemplate all questions and comments received after 5:00 PM CDT on 26 October 2026. Industry participants are encouraged to clearly identify each submission as either a Question or Comment. Submissions containing both should distinguish the questions requiring Government responses from comments provided solely for consideration. The Government appreciates industry's participation and welcomes constructive feedback to support development of a clear, competitive, and commercially viable Final AOI. The following represents the anticipated Final AOI SAM.gov description: MACH1 Area of Interest: F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB, Rapid Delivery Progressive Design-Build The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS), in coordination with the Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC), is seeking highly qualified Design-Build teams to deliver the Rapid Delivery Projects supporting the F-47 mission at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, utilizing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model. This Area of Interest (AOI) is issued under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice, FA8903-OT-MACH1. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Respondents shall comply with the MACH1 Umbrella Program Notice and the project-specific requirements established in the attached AOI. Program Overview The F-47 Campus at Nellis AFB is an approximately $1.057 billion total programmed military construction initiative intended to provide the facilities and infrastructure necessary to support the F-47 mission. This amount includes construction, contingency, design, construction security, and other applicable project costs and does not represent the construction agreement value available under this AOI. The present acquisition contemplates award for the Rapid Delivery Projects under Milestones 2 through 4 only, consisting of: Combined Operations and Maintenance Hangar. Reprogramming Laboratory. Simulator Facility. Aircraft Apron with Sunshades. Supporting utilities and infrastructure necessary for permanent operation of the Rapid Delivery facilities. The Government strongly prefers to select one Design-Build team capable of delivering all Rapid Delivery Projects, while reserving the right to select up to four teams if warranted by program requirements and permitted by the applicable acquisition authority. The Government also values organizations possessing the qualifications and resources to support the remaining Nellis F-47 Campus. However, selection under this AOI does not guarantee Milestone 5 or subsequent Agreement(s). Progressive Design-Build Delivery Approach The Government intends to initiate design and preconstruction services following completion of the Planning Charrette Reports establishing the initial mission requirements. The selected Design-Build team will work collaboratively with AFCEC and its Owner's Advisor to advance facility designs, evaluate alternative technical and construction solutions, develop cost and schedule strategies, and establish commercially supportable construction pricing. The Government contemplates negotiating firm-fixed-price construction agreement at approximately 65% design completion, subject to sufficient scope maturity, risk allocation, and commercial cost viability. Advanced design packages, early construction activities, and long-lead procurement may be considered where appropriately justified and authorized. AFCEC seeks a collaborative construction partner committed to delivering the greatest possible mission capability and value for the resources invested. The Government intends to consider innovative design and construction approaches, including industrialized construction methods, commercially effective Agreement commitment strategies, and practical alternatives that improve affordability and schedule performance. Three-Phase Selection Process The Government intends to conduct an expedited three-phase selection process under MACH1: Phase 1: Solution Brief. Respondents will submit qualifications and technical information demonstrating the capabilities of their actual proposed design and construction organizations. The attached AOI establishes ten project-specific technical factors and a maximum of 20 narrative pages, with separately permitted appendices. No construction price or rough-order-of-magnitude construction estimate is required during Phase 1 Submissions. Phase 2: Oral Presentations / Pitch Sessions. Selected respondents will be invited to participate in oral presentations. Detailed instructions and additional technical information will be provided to invited respondents, subject to applicable information-security requirements. Phase 3: Full Phase 3 Submission and Negotiations. The Government intends to conduct direct negotiations with selected respondent(s), subject to applicable authority and Agreements Officer approval. title: Tattoo Removal Services- Sources Sought ONLY
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking qualified contractors to provide onsite laser tattoo removal services at multiple federal correctional institutions. The contractor shall furnish all personnel, FDA-approved laser equipment, supplies, transportation, training, documentation, and related support necessary to perform tattoo removal services for eligible inmates. Services include consultation, treatment, documentation of procedures and outcomes, follow-up recommendations, and compliance with all applicable federal, state, medical, safety, and security requirements. Personnel must possess all required certifications, licenses, and experience necessary to perform professional tattoo removal services in accordance with applicable laws and regulations. The requirement includes services at multiple BOP institutions in Arizona, Florida, Indiana, and Pennsylvania, with potential expansion to additional locations. Contractors should carefully consider the geographic distribution of performance locations and demonstrate their ability to support all locations identified in the requirement. Respondents shall identify any planned subcontracting arrangements and provide examples of tattoo removal services performed directly by their organization as the prime contractor. Experience performed solely by subcontractors or teaming partners should be separately identified. Any future small business set-aside acquisition resulting from this requirement will be subject to the applicable limitations on subcontracting requirements of FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR �125.6. Respondents should describe how they would comply with these requirements if awarded a contract. Vendors should carefully review the SOW before submitting a response. The Government is seeking capability information from firms that can directly perform and support the full scope of services across all identified performance locations. Responses that do not address the firm's ability to meet the requirements outlined in the SOW may be considered less useful for market research purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. The Government is conducting market research to identify qualified contractors capable of providing professional tattoo removal services. The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability of capable small business concerns, including socioeconomic small business categories, and to assist the Government in developing an appropriate acquisition strategy and potential set-aside determination. Responses to this notice are voluntary and shall not be considered offers. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this Sources Sought Notice and will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Interested vendors are requested to provide: Company name and address UEI number Business size and socioeconomic status Relevant NAICS code(s) SAM.gov registration status Description of experience providing tattoo removal services Description of equipment, certifications, licensing, and personnel qualifications Geographic service capabilities Any recommended contract structure or acquisition considerations The Government may use information received in response to this notice for acquisition planning purposes only. Participation in this market research effort is not a prerequisite for participation in any future solicitation.

title: Germany – Underground work other than tunnels, shafts and subways – Stadt Drolshagen - Bauliche Erweiterung der Gräfin-Sayn-Verbundgrundschule zum Ausbau der Ganztagsbetreuung am Hauptstandort Drolshagen | Tiefbauarbeiten 1. Bauabschnitt
description: Für die Bestandsgebäude der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule in Drolshagen besteht ein baulicher, funktionaler sowie teilweise energetischer Sanierungsbedarf. Zudem ist eine Anpassung an aktuelle pädagogische Anforderungen sowie an moderne Nutzungs- und Raumkonzepte vorgesehen. Im Zuge der geplanten Maßnahmen werden Umbau-, Modernisierungs-, Sanierungs- sowie Teilabbruch- und Erweiterungsmaßnahmen erforderlich. Die Liegenschaftsadresse lautet: Gräfin-Sayn-Schule Am Buscheid 2 57489 Drolshagen Gebäudebeschreibung: Die bestehende Schulanlage der Gräfin-Sayn-Schule besteht aus mehreren miteinander verbundenen bzw. separaten Gebäudeteilen unterschiedlicher Baujahre. Die Gebäude umfassen: • Unterrichts- und Klassenräume • Verwaltungs- und Nebenräume • Sanitärbereiche • Fachräume sowie ergänzende Nutzflächen Die Gebäude sind teilweise mehrgeschossig ausgeführt und über befestigte Schulhofflächen sowie interne Wege miteinander verbunden. Die Außenanlagen bestehen überwiegend aus: • asphaltierten Schulhofflächen • befestigten Zugangs- und Verkehrsflächen • Grün- und Aufenthaltsbereichen Neues Nutzungskonzept: Im Rahmen der geplanten Baumaßnahme wird die bestehende Schulanlage abschnittsweise weiterentwickelt und modernisiert. Die Maßnahmen umfassen insbesondere: • Teilabbruch einzelner Gebäudebereiche, die den heutigen Anforderungen nicht mehr entsprechen • Sanierung und Modernisierung von Bestandsgebäuden, insbesondere im Hinblick auf: • energetische Verbesserung (Dach, Fassade, Fenster) • funktionale Anpassung der Grundrisse • brandschutztechnische Ertüchtigung • Umbauarbeiten im Innenbereich zur Anpassung an das aktuelle Raumprogramm • Ergänzende Neubau- bzw. Erweiterungsmaßnahmen Die Bauausführung erfolgt in mehreren Bauabschnitten, um den Schulbetrieb aufrechtzuerhalten. Die auszuschreibende Leistung betrifft die Tiefbauarbeiten für den 1. Bauabschnitt.

title: Germany – Photocopier paper and xerographic paper – Rahmenvereinbarung über die Lieferung von Kopier- und Spezialpapier an die Landeshauptstadt Mainz mit 12 monatiger Vertragslaufzeit, voraussichtlich ab 01.01.2027
description: Die Landeshauptstadt Mainz beabsichtigt den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung über eine Laufzeit von 12 Monaten und einer automatischen Auftragsverlängerung über weitere 12 Monate. Gegenstand dieser Rahmenvereinbarung ist die Lieferung von unterschiedlichen Kopier- und Spezialpapieren aufgrund von einzelnen Abrufaufträgen der bestellberechtigten Organisationseinheiten. Hierzu zählen neben städtischen Ämtern und Eigenbetrieben insbesondere auch Kindertagesstätten und Schulen sowie stadtnahe Gesellschaften und Anstalten des öffentlichen Rechts. Die einzelnen Abrufaufträge erfolgen über einen elektronischen Einkaufskatalog, den ein Dienstleister betreibt. Die von der Rahmenvereinbarung umfassten Produkte sind daher im elektronischen Einkaufskatalog einzustellen, um abgerufen werden zu können.

Erweiterungsmaßnahmen Die Bauausführung erfolgt in mehreren Bauabschnitten, um den Schulbetrieb aufrechtzuerhalten. Die auszuschreibende Leistung betrifft die Tiefbauarbeiten für den 1. Bauabschnitt.

title: Finland – Public road transport services – TRAFICOM /Reittipohjaiset joukkoliikennepalvelut, brutto, tarjouskilpailu 2026/13
description: Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto Traficom (jäljempänä Traficom) pyytää tarjoustanne joukkoliikennepalveluiden hoitamisesta. Tarkemmat kohteet ja sopimuskaudet on nähtävissä tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Liikenne hankitaan bruttosopimuksella. Bruttosopimuksella tarkoitetaan palvelusopimusasetuksen (1370 /2007) ja erityisalojen hankintalain (1398/2016) tarkoittamaa joukkoliikenteen palvelusopimusta, jossa lipputuloriski on liikenteen tilaajalla. Hankinnasta syntyvien sopimusten rahoitukseen voi osallistua hankintayksikkönä toimivan Traficomin lisäksi lisäksi kunnat, kaupungit, hyvinvointialueet, oppilaitokset sekä toimivaltaiset viranomaiset. Tämän hankinnan sisältämälle liikenteelle myönnetään palvelusopimusasetuksen mukainen yksinoikeus erillisellä hallinnollisella päätöksellä. Yksinoikeuspäätöksessä otetaan huomioon mahdollinen reitin osan läpi kulkeva pidempimatkainen liikenne. Lippu- ja maksujärjestelmävaatimukset sekä liikennepalvelulain (320/2017) edellyttämät yhteentoimivuusvaatimukset on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä.

title: Request for Information _ Creation of The United States Space Academy
description: On Aug. 28, 2026, President Donald J. Trump issued Executive Order (E.O.) 14423, Establishing the United States Space Academy. To answer that call, the United States Space Academy (USSA) is envisioned as a NASA-led, civilian Federal academic institution that combines rigorous technical education with disciplined leadership development, civic responsibility, and a lasting commitment to public service. The Academy will prepare future scientists, engineers, astronauts, pilots, operators, entrepreneurs, civil servants, warfighters, and other leaders to advance American interests across the aerospace sector. Through this Request for Information (RFI), NASA invites each State to submit one official State-sponsored response prepared by a �Responding Entity� and coordinated and formally endorsed by a State Selecting Official. The Governor must designate both the Responding Entity and the State Selecting Official in writing. The response should provide information to support NASA�s assessment of potential locations and operating solutions for the United States Space Academy (USSA). That assessment will inform NASA�s recommendation to the Commission. NASA�s objectives for this announcement are to: Identify potential locations for the permanent establishment of the USSA campus, including a groundbreaking no later than 2027. Identify interim solutions that may allow the USSA to begin instruction in 2028 and facilitate a smooth transition to a permanent campus by 2031. Explore the estimated costs of establishing the USSA and potential state, local, and other non-Federal partnerships that could support its establishment. Information obtained through this RFI will be used by NASA and the Commission to develop the recommended process for selecting the Academy�s permanent physical location, which will be reported to the President for decision. A separate announcement for formal proposals may be issued at a later date. UPDATES MADE AS OF 10.2.26: Question and Answers Document attached.
